title: Weak excluded middle and directed future cones

based_on.title: Intuitionistic Logic, Winter 2019/20 (notes dated January 2, 2020)
based_on.pages: §1.8, printed p.25, Example23; §2, printed pp.26–27, axiom schemas and KC

summary: Characterize weak excluded middle by directed future cones, derive its De Morgan form, and separate schema validity from truth in one model.
abstract: An undecided statement may become true later without being true now. Weak excluded middle allows that possibility while saying that a statement is either permanently impossible or remains attainable beyond every future stage. We show that this principle holds for every valuation precisely when any two futures of one world can share a continuation. In a finite rooted partial order this requires a greatest world, but infinite frames behave differently. Adding the principle as ordinary assumptions gives exactly the same deductions as the missing constructive direction of De Morgan’s law. Explicit chain and fork models show why the principle is stronger than intuitionistic logic yet weaker than full excluded middle, and why one successful valuation cannot determine a frame’s logic.
